title: Sixth Word The Two Mens Responses And Outcomes

questions.question: What situation did the king create for the two men at the beginning of the passage?
questions.answer: He placed each of them in charge of an estate with equipment, animals, and tools.

questions.question: Why was the condition of those estates uncertain?
questions.answer: The time was full of conflict and unrest, so things could easily be ruined or changed.

questions.question: How did the king communicate his offer to the two men?
questions.answer: He sent a respected representative with a merciful message.

questions.question: What did the king ask the two men to do with the property in their care?
questions.answer: He asked them to hand it over to him willingly so he could protect it for them.

questions.question: What promise did the king make about the property after the time of war ended?
questions.answer: He promised to return it in a better state than before.

questions.question: Besides returning it, what else did the king promise to give for the property?
questions.answer: He promised a very great payment for it.

questions.question: What did the king say would happen to the workshop tools if the men accepted his offer?
questions.answer: The tools would be used for the king’s service, and their return and benefit would greatly increase.

questions.question: Why did the king say he should take responsibility for expenses and supplies?
questions.answer: The two men were too poor and unable to cover the cost of such major work themselves.

questions.question: How many kinds of gain did the king say the men would receive if they accepted?
questions.answer: Five kinds of gain.

questions.question: What losses did the king warn about if they refused?
questions.answer: They would lose the property, miss the high payment, see valuable things become useless, carry the burden of managing them, and face punishment for breaking trust.

questions.question: What new status would a man receive if he accepted the king’s offer?
questions.answer: He would serve as the king’s soldier in an honorable and free position instead of a low and restricted one.

questions.question: How did the wiser of the two men respond to the king’s message?
questions.answer: He gladly accepted and expressed strong gratitude.

questions.question: What character traits are given for the man who refused?
questions.answer: He was proud, self-centered, wasteful, and controlled by his lower desires.

questions.question: What false idea seems to have influenced the man who refused?
questions.answer: He acted as if he would remain on the estate forever.

questions.question: How did the second man answer the king’s offer?
questions.answer: He rejected it and chose his own enjoyment over obedience.

questions.question: What was the result for the first man after some time passed?
questions.answer: He rose to a very high rank, gained the king’s favor, and lived in happiness.

questions.question: What happened to the second man in the end?
questions.answer: He lost both his comfort and his property and fell into punishment and suffering.

questions.question: Who are the main figures in the comparison found in this passage?
questions.answer: A king, his messenger, and two men entrusted with estates.

questions.question: What does the word “entrusted” suggest about the estates?
questions.answer: It suggests the men were caretakers, not absolute owners.

questions.question: Why is that detail important for understanding the king’s request?
questions.answer: It shows the king was asking for something that already truly belonged to him.

questions.question: What does the unstable setting add to the meaning of the king’s offer?
questions.answer: It makes the offer look wise and merciful because the property was in danger anyway.

questions.question: In what way was the king’s message compassionate?
questions.answer: He offered protection, reward, and support instead of simply taking back what was his.

questions.question: How does the king try to persuade the men logically?
questions.answer: He explains both the benefits of accepting and the harms of refusing.

questions.question: What practical problem of the two men does the king mention directly?
questions.answer: They lack the means and strength to manage the heavy costs themselves.

questions.question: What does the king’s willingness to cover expenses show about his generosity?
questions.answer: It shows he gives help in addition to reward, not just commands.

questions.question: Why would accepting the offer remove anxiety from the men?
questions.answer: They would no longer have to fear losing or preserving what they could not really secure.

questions.question: What does the king mean by saying the tools would be used in his name?
questions.answer: Their work would become part of the king’s service rather than private use.

questions.question: Why is becoming the king’s soldier better than remaining a common captive or irregular fighter?
questions.answer: It brings dignity, freedom, and closeness to royal service.

questions.question: Which man is presented as truly intelligent, and how can you tell?
questions.answer: The one who accepted, because he recognized the value of the offer and responded with thanks.

questions.question: What inner weakness kept the second man from making the wise choice?
questions.answer: His arrogance and selfish desire for temporary pleasure blinded him.

questions.question: How does the passage connect pride with poor judgment?
questions.answer: The proud man ignores danger and refuses a beneficial offer because he is full of himself.

questions.question: Why is the second man’s choice unrealistic?
questions.answer: He behaves as though worldly things will last forever even though the passage says they do not.

questions.question: What was the final social result of each man’s decision?
questions.answer: People admired the first man and pitied the second.

questions.question: What did each of the two men receive from the king?
questions.answer: Each one was given charge over an estate filled with what was needed for work and defense.

questions.question: What does the troubled period in the story suggest about worldly possessions?
questions.answer: They are unstable and can quickly be lost or changed.

questions.question: Why did the king send a lieutenant instead of coming personally in the story?
questions.answer: The lieutenant served as the royal messenger delivering the king’s order and mercy.

questions.question: What was the king trying to prevent by asking for the property back?
questions.answer: He wanted to keep it from being wasted or destroyed without benefit.

questions.question: How would the men benefit from the king’s care of the property even before its return?
questions.answer: They would still receive income and profit while the king handled the burden.

questions.question: What does the king’s offer reveal about the relationship between ownership and trust?
questions.answer: Real ownership remains with the king, while the men only hold the property temporarily.

questions.question: Why is the offered payment described as high?
questions.answer: It shows the king rewards them far beyond what they could expect.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the king saying the use of the tools would increase greatly in value?
questions.answer: Their ordinary work would gain much greater worth when tied to the king’s service.

questions.question: Why would refusal lead to both hardship and punishment?
questions.answer: The men would struggle to guard what they could not keep and also be guilty of betraying what was entrusted to them.

questions.question: What kind of reasoning does the first man use in accepting the offer?
questions.answer: He sees that accepting is both honorable and profitable.

questions.question: What kind of reasoning does the second man use in refusing it?
questions.answer: He follows desire and pride rather than truth and consequences.

questions.question: How does the passage show that selfish pleasure can be spiritually dangerous?
questions.answer: The second man rejects lasting good because he does not want his enjoyment interrupted.

questions.question: What image in the passage shows the second man was detached from reality?
questions.answer: He acted like he would remain forever in a place clearly threatened by disaster.

questions.question: How are the outcomes of the two men opposite to one another?
questions.answer: One gains rank, nearness, and joy, while the other loses status, possessions, and peace.

questions.question: What does the first man’s life in the king’s palace suggest symbolically within the story itself?
questions.answer: It suggests acceptance brought honor, security, and a special relationship with the king.

questions.question: What does the second man’s torment show about the cost of rejecting mercy?
questions.answer: Refusing a generous offer can turn opportunity into punishment.

questions.question: What important responsibility did the two men share at the start of the story?
questions.answer: Both were responsible for managing property placed in their care by the king.

questions.question: What details show that the estates were valuable?
questions.answer: They included productive and useful items like workshops, equipment, mounts, and weapons.

questions.question: Why did the dangerous age make the king’s offer urgent?
questions.answer: Delay could mean the estates would be ruined before any good came from them.

questions.question: What tone does the king use in his message?
questions.answer: He speaks with mercy, concern, and generosity.

questions.question: Why is the phrase about keeping the property for them important?
questions.answer: It shows the king is not trying to deprive them but to preserve their benefit.

questions.question: What two things did the king promise concerning labor and reward?
questions.answer: He would direct the work and also multiply the return from it.

questions.question: What weakness of the two men is stated openly by the king?
questions.answer: They do not have the resources to handle the full cost and demands of the task.

questions.question: How does the king’s proposal combine kindness with authority?
questions.answer: He offers help and reward, yet also warns of consequences for disobedience.

questions.question: Why would refusing the offer be foolish even from a worldly point of view?
questions.answer: The property was already at risk, and refusal would only add burden without securing it.

questions.question: What happens to valuable tools if they are not put to the right use in the story?
questions.answer: They lose their worth and end up wasted.

questions.question: What does the first man’s thankful response reveal about his character?
questions.answer: He is humble, perceptive, and appreciative.

questions.question: What does the second man’s response reveal about his character?
questions.answer: He is arrogant, attached to pleasure, and blind to reality.

questions.question: Why is the second man’s attachment to enjoyment presented negatively?
questions.answer: It leads him to ignore truth, responsibility, and his own future.

questions.question: What does the story suggest about temporary enjoyment compared with lasting reward?
questions.answer: Chasing short pleasure can make a person miss far greater and longer-lasting good.

questions.question: How is the first man honored after accepting the king’s terms?
questions.answer: He rises in status and is welcomed into the king’s own residence.

questions.question: What emotional reaction do people have toward the second man at the end?
questions.answer: They feel pity for him, though they also recognize that he brought it on himself.

questions.question: What is the basic conflict in this passage?
questions.answer: The two men must choose whether to surrender a temporary trust to the king or cling to it for themselves.

questions.question: Why is the king’s request reasonable based on the story?
questions.answer: The property belongs to him originally, and he offers to protect and reward the men for giving it back.

questions.question: What conditions in the story make private control unreliable?
questions.answer: The land is full of upheaval, war, and instability.

questions.question: What does the king promise to do with the trust while the men wait for the end of the conflict?
questions.answer: He promises to preserve it, improve it, and let them keep its returns.

questions.question: What does the king’s offer teach about giving up control?
questions.answer: Giving up control to the rightful owner can actually bring greater safety and gain.

questions.question: Why are the men not in a good position to insist on independence?
questions.answer: They are poor and unable to carry the expenses of the work.

questions.question: How does the king strengthen his argument by discussing both profit and loss?
questions.answer: He shows that acceptance leads to multiple benefits while refusal leads to multiple harms.

questions.question: What honorable role is offered in place of a lowly one?
questions.answer: Service as the king’s own soldier in a respected position.

questions.question: How does the first man understand the offer differently from the second?
questions.answer: He sees it as a blessing, while the second sees it as a threat to his personal pleasure.

questions.question: What is the effect of arrogance on the second man’s judgment?
questions.answer: It keeps him from recognizing his dependence and his danger.

questions.question: What phrase in meaning best describes the second man’s outlook on life?
questions.answer: He lives as if the world and his enjoyment will never end.

questions.question: Why is gratitude linked with wisdom in the first man?
questions.answer: His thankfulness shows he recognizes both the king’s generosity and his own need.

questions.question: What final reward does the first man receive that goes beyond money or property?
questions.answer: He gains closeness to the king and a life of honor.

questions.question: What does the second man lose besides material things?
questions.answer: He loses happiness, dignity, and peace.

questions.question: Why is the second man’s suffering presented as deserved?
questions.answer: He knowingly rejected a generous and beneficial offer out of pride.

questions.question: What does the story imply about responsibility toward what is placed in our care?
questions.answer: We must treat it as a trust and respond rightly to the one who gave it.

questions.question: At the opening of the passage, what did the king place under the care of each man?
questions.answer: A full estate with the means needed for work and protection.

questions.question: What larger condition threatened everything in the story?
questions.answer: A violent and unstable age in which possessions could not remain secure.

questions.question: What does the king’s sending of a noble lieutenant suggest about the message?
questions.answer: It was official, important, and delivered with honor.

questions.question: What was the main action the king requested from the two men?
questions.answer: He asked them to transfer the trust back to him.

questions.question: What future benefit did the king attach to this action?
questions.answer: He would later restore the property in an improved form.

questions.question: What immediate financial benefit did the king also promise?
questions.answer: A rich payment and increased return from the tools and work.

questions.question: How did the king address the men’s inability to carry out expensive tasks?
questions.answer: He said he would provide the needed costs and equipment himself.

questions.question: Why was this offer especially generous?
questions.answer: The king not only relieved them of burden but also allowed them to keep the gains.

questions.question: What warning did the king give about trying to hold the property on their own?
questions.answer: They would fail to keep it and end up losing both it and the offered reward.

questions.question: What moral failure would refusal involve according to the king?
questions.answer: It would be an abuse of entrusted property.

questions.question: What social and political promotion comes with acceptance?
questions.answer: The man becomes an honored servant of the king instead of remaining low-ranking.

questions.question: Which of the two men responds with humility?
questions.answer: The one who gladly accepts and gives thanks.

questions.question: Which of the two men is ruled by his lower self?
questions.answer: The one who refuses because of pride and attachment to pleasure.

questions.question: What mistaken view of time shapes the second man’s refusal?
questions.answer: He behaves as though his stay and possessions are permanent.

questions.question: What happened to the first man after his acceptance?
questions.answer: He rose in rank and enjoyed a joyful life near the king.

questions.question: What happened to the second man after his rejection?
questions.answer: He sank into misery, lost what he had, and suffered punishment.

questions.question: How do other people react to the final condition of each man?
questions.answer: They envy the first and pity the second.
